paper_metadata.title: Minimizing estimation runtime on noisy quantum computers

summary: The paper introduces engineered likelihood functions (ELFs) to accelerate expectation-value estimation in hybrid quantum algorithms. Simulations with circuit depth L=6 and layer fidelity p=0.9 show significantly faster RMSE decay than standard sampling and Chebyshev likelihood functions, while the theoretical model predicts runtime scaling improving from O(1/ε²) (classical sampling) toward O(1/ε) as device coherence improves.

experiments.description: Ancilla-free engineered likelihood function (ELF) amplitude-estimation / expectation-value estimation with Bayesian inference, compared against standard sampling and Chebyshev likelihood functions (CLF), using fixed circuit depth and varying fidelity/true expectation value in simulation.

algorithm.variant: ancilla-free engineered likelihood function (AF ELF) with Bayesian inference
algorithm.ansatz: state-preparation circuit A and its inverse A†; generalized reflections U(x)=exp(-ixP) and V(y)=AR0(y)A†
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bayesian inference iterated until convergence criterion satisfied; simulation uses fixed L per run
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initial point for parameter-tuning algorithms; prior over Π from standard sampling or domain knowledge

optimizer_settings.step_size_schedule: δ(t) for gradient ascent (not numerically specified)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Expectation value Π=⟨A|P|A⟩ of a Hermitian ±1 observable P on state |A⟩; no explicit QUBO/Ising encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Π=⟨A|P|A⟩ (equivalently θ=arccos(Π)) with reduced measurement/runtime cost

problem_instance.description: Generic expectation-value estimation / amplitude-estimation benchmark; no specific application instance in the reported simulations

dataset_specification.description: Simulation studies over chosen true Π values and Gaussian priors

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 300 independent simulation runs per configuration; RMSE over time; fixed L and p in main comparisons

quantum_resources.gate_fidelity: two-qubit gate fidelity 99.92% mentioned as near-term example; layer fidelity p=0.9 in main simulations

noise_model.noise_type: exponential decay likelihood-function noise model; depolarizing layer noise; SPAM error model
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: likelihood-function calibration / noise-tailoring discussed conceptually; no explicit mitigation protocol in experiments

noise_parameters.fidelity_f: f= p^L (with no SPAM error in experiments)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: lookup table of optimal circuit parameters over a discrete Π grid; sinusoidal fitting of likelihood near current prior mean
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bayesian update with Gaussian approximation; convert θ posterior to Π posterior via cos(θ)

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: RMSE decreases over time; inverse MSE approximately linear in time for fixed depth

results.value: approximately linear inverse-MSE growth in time

results.unit: queries to ansatz circuit A / A†

results.value: 2L+1 per inference round; with L=6 this is 13 ansatz invocations per round

speedup_claims.conditions: in the low-noise regime and with engineered likelihood functions / enhanced sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes interpolation between O(1/epsilon^2) and O(1/epsilon) depending on noise; not all settings achieve the Heisenberg limit.

speedup_claims.factor: AF ELF and AB ELF outperform CLF; AF ELF best in all reported cases
speedup_claims.baseline_method: Chebyshev likelihood function (CLF) and standard sampling
speedup_claims.conditions: fixed L=6, p=0.9, no SPAM error, synthetic expectation-value estimation tasks
speedup_claims.caveats: Performance depends on true Pi for CLF; ELF is more stable across Pi.

speedup_claims.conditions: as a function of noise parameter lambda
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a model-derived asymptotic interpolation, not a direct hardware benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: sample/runtime scaling interpolates between O(1/ε) (Heisenberg limit, phase-estimation–like regime) and O(1/ε^2) (standard sampling/VQE regime)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: standard sampling O(1/ε^2) for expectation estimation

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not specified; runtime model predicts crossover depending on noise parameter λ and target precision ε
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Model example assumes ~100 logical qubits, circuit layer depth ~200 two‑qubit gates, two‑qubit gate fidelity approaching ≥99.9999 with error correction to reach useful runtimes
limiting_factors: All results produced via classical simulation rather than QPU execution
Speedup is only quadratic in precision (O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε^2))
Large measurement counts and circuit depths required
Requires high gate fidelity or error correction to realize theoretical gains
No concrete application instance benchmarked against classical state‑of‑the‑art algorithms

notes: No specific QPU or vendor is named; experiments are simulation-based, so hardware.type inferred as simulator_other.
Ancilla-free scheme uses no ancilla qubits; num_qubits not explicitly stated because the paper focuses on logical subspace and circuit structure rather than a concrete register size.
Authors discuss potential quantum speedups but provide only simulated estimation experiments and theoretical runtime models; no empirical quantum advantage demonstration.
